newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea watchdog unions vow to strike over reform.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea watchdog unions vow to strike over reform.

text.p: Unionised workers at South Korea's financial watchdog bodies on Tuesday vowed to go on strike unless the government dropped a plan to integrate those organisations into one under the prime minister.
"If the government ignores our demand, we all go on strike and seek to resign en masse," said Kim Yang-koo, union chairman of the Securities Supervisory Board (SSB).

Union leaders of the SSB, the central Bank of Korea and the Insurance Supervisory Board said in a press conference those three watchdog bodies should retain their supervisory authority in light of their specialties.
"They should be guaranteed autonomy as independent organisations," union leaders said in a statement.
A union spokesman at the central bank said no date had been set for a strike. "We will make every effort to change the government's mind before actually going on strike," he said.
Union outrage flared following Monday's announcement by Finance Minister Kang Kyong-shik that the existing watchdog bodies would be melded into a single government organisation.
Labour unions argued the government was trying to gain control over the whole financial industry in an election year.
But analysts played down the union's accusations and said workers were really worried about losing their jobs as a result of integration of the watchdog bodies.
They said it was a global trend that barriers between financial sectors were falling and the basic idea of integrating the supervisory functions was well in line with this trend.

Minister Kang said there would be no job cuts "in the process of integrating the supervisory bodies", but did not elaborate how all the existing workforce would be absorbed into a single organisation.
